summary.en: Update a rolling hash for each text window and verify equal hashes so collisions never become false matches.
summary.bn: প্রতি উইন্ডোর rolling hash আপডেট করো, আর হ্যাশ মিললেও অক্ষর দেখে নিশ্চিত হও যেন ভুল ম্যাচ না আসে।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

sections.title: Use a fingerprint to filter windows
Give every digit a place value
A window exists only when it fits
A hash hit must not increment the answer alone
Small modular products fit C17 int

examples.title: Search with verified rolling hashes
examples.explanationHtml: The main program reports two hash hits and two true matches for ababa and aba. For text dx and pattern aa, it reports one hash hit but count zero. Direct verification determines the answer.

examples.title: Exhibit a real collision
examples.explanationHtml: The second example prints the equal hashes of aa and dx under the exact teaching formula. It makes the need for verification concrete rather than treating collisions as a remote possibility.

examples.title: Inspect each short window hash
examples.explanationHtml: For length-two windows of ababa, the last program prints hashes 1,26,1,26. Equal windows repeat their hashes. This example isolates the rolling update so its arithmetic is easier to inspect.

practice.title: Show a real collision using base 26, modulus 101, and a=0.
practice.statementHtml: Show a real collision using base 26, modulus 101, and a=0.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: aa hashes to zero. dx has digit values 3 and 23, giving 3*26+23=101, also zero modulo 101. A direct comparison rejects dx when searching for aa.

practice.title: Derive the rolling update for the next length-m window.
practice.statementHtml: Derive the rolling update for the next length-m window.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The old hash weights its leading digit by high=base^(m-1) mod q. Subtract leading*high and normalize modulo q. Multiply by base to shift remaining digits left, then add the incoming digit and reduce again.

quiz.prompt: What does a hash equality prove in verified Rabin-Karp?
quiz.explanation: Collisions exist, so equality identifies only a candidate.

quiz.prompt: Which factor removes the outgoing character contribution?
quiz.explanation: The leading digit occupies the highest power in a length-m hash.
It is a hash candidate rejected by direct comparison.

quiz.prompt: Why normalize the subtraction in C?
options: A negative dividend can have a negative remainder
quiz.explanation: C remainder keeps the dividend sign, so add the modulus when needed.

quiz.prompt: For a=0 and base=26 modulo 101, which pair collides?
quiz.explanation: dx represents 3*26+23=101, congruent to the zero hash of aa.

quiz.prompt: What is the verified worst-case search bound for 1<=m<=n?
quiz.explanation: Many hash hits can each require m character comparisons.

quiz.prompt: Which condition supports near-linear expected performance?
options: Few spurious hits under suitable hash assumptions
A fixed small modulus guarantees it
quiz.explanation: Good hashing makes unnecessary verifications uncommon; the fixed teaching modulus is not an adversarial guarantee.

quiz.prompt: Which rolling hash does dx have under base 26 modulo 101?
quiz.explanation: The polynomial value is exactly 101, leaving remainder zero.

quiz.prompt: What does C print for the negative remainder and its normalized version?
quiz.explanation: C gives negative three, while adding the modulus normalizes it to two.

quiz.prompt: When hash 1 for ab rolls forward to ba, what value appears?
quiz.explanation: Removing a contributes zero; multiplying the remaining b digit by 26 gives 26.

keyPoints.en: A rolling hash removes one leading digit and appends one new digit.
keyPoints.bn: rolling hash-এ সামনের অক্ষরের অবদান সরিয়ে নতুন অক্ষর যোগ করো।

keyPoints.en: Equal strings have equal hashes, but the converse can fail.
keyPoints.bn: একই স্ট্রিংয়ের হ্যাশ একই; হ্যাশ এক হলেও স্ট্রিং আলাদা হতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Verify each hash hit with character comparisons.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি hash hit-এ অক্ষর মিলিয়ে নিশ্চিত হও।

keyPoints.en: Normalize a negative remainder before the next hash update.
keyPoints.bn: পরের হ্যাশ আপডেটের আগে ঋণাত্মক remainder ঠিক করো।

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and justify the time and space costs of Rabin-Karp Algorithm.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
The hash invariant states that window equals the polynomial of text[start..start+m), reduced modulo q. Initial construction establishes it for start zero. Removing the highest-power outgoing digit leaves the suffix polynomial. Multiplication by base shifts its exponents up, and appending the incoming digit constructs the next window. Modular arithmetic preserves each equality of residues.

If a text window equals the pattern, their digit sequences and polynomial values agree, so their hashes agree. The hash filter therefore never rejects a true occurrence. When hashes agree, direct comparison accepts exactly the equal windows. Together those facts prove both completeness and soundness of the reported matches.

Collisions do not invalidate the invariant. They mean the polynomial map is many-to-one. The exactness of this version comes from verification, not from assuming a sufficiently large prime eliminates all collisions.

A double hash makes accidental collisions less likely under suitable assumptions, but two fixed hashes still do not prove equality for arbitrary strings. If an application omits verification, it must accept a probabilistic or collision-dependent correctness policy. That is a different design from the exact matcher shown here.

Constructing the pattern hash, first window and highest power takes O(m). Rolling through legal starts takes O(n). If H windows have equal hashes, verifying them adds up to O(H*m). A precise bound is therefore O(n+m+H*m).

Under a suitable randomised hash choice and a nonadversarial model, spurious hits can be rare, giving near-linear expected filtering work. Real matches still need verification in this implementation. A text of repeated a letters and a pattern of repeated a letters creates many true hits, each scanning m positions.

Thus verified Rabin-Karp has O(nm) worst-case time when m<=n. A fixed small modulus does not supply a universal near-linear guarantee. Always state the hash assumptions behind an expected-time claim.

The working hash values and counters require O(1) auxiliary space beyond input strings. Retaining all match positions adds O(z) output storage. The examples print positions immediately. Their fixed buffers are bounded teaching storage rather than a different mathematical space claim.

For matching many patterns of the same length, hash buckets can filter against several candidates together. Every equal-hash candidate still needs verification. Different pattern lengths require separate window lengths or another indexing strategy; one rolling value cannot represent every length at once.
